Balanced-positive with caution. The rate cut to 1.50–1.75% and IOER at 1.55%, alongside T-bill purchases and repo operations to maintain “ample” reserves, signal an accommodative stance aimed at sustaining the expansion amid muted inflation and weak business fixed investment and exports. The literature supports this reading: the interest-rate channel should modestly bolster business fixed investment and inventory accumulation (investment depends on interest rates; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994 highlight the strong linkage to internal funds and liquidity), while New Keynesian frameworks (Galí and Gertler 1999; Woodford 2003; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans 2005) emphasize the role of expectations and the policy rate in steering inflation back toward target when inflation is below 2% and market-based compensation is low. Empirical work (Romer and Romer; Sims) documents that monetary policy shocks influence output and investment, consistent with the Committee’s goal of supporting continued growth. However, the explicit mention of “uncertainties,” persistent softness in capital spending and trade, and two dissents temper the tone. Net effect: slightly positive sentiment, but not exuberant.

“This action supports the Committee’s view that sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee’s symmetric 2 percent objective are the most likely outcomes, but uncertainties about this outlook remain.”
